newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TML sees 97/98 growth for established units.
newsitem.headline: TML sees 97/98 growth for established units.

text.p: South African media group Times Media Ltd (TML) said on Monday its established operations should continue to show real growth in the new financial year provided business confidence remains strong.
At the same time losses from existing new ventures should decline in the coming year, TML said in a statement accompanying its year end results.
"Business confidence seems to have improved in recent months. Provided this continues, the established operations should continue to show real growth," the firm said.
It said it would continue to pursue expansion opportunities, both organically and by acquisition.
TML earlier released year headline earnings up a slim seven percent to 275 cents a share, well below analysts' forecasts of a rise to between 302 and 304 cents.
The total dividend at 130 cents a share was slightly below expectations of between 132 and 135 cents.

TML said the results were not directly comparable with the previous year as turnover and operating profit for the last two months of the year under review included only 50 percent of the results for core publications, Business Day and Financial Mail.
With effect from February 1 these operations were sold to a new company BDFM Publishers (Pty) Ltd, jointly owned by TML and U.K-based Pearson Plc.
In addition this deal gave rise to a one-off profit of 80.4 million rand which has been shown as an exceptional item.

TML said the noticeable slowdown in the economy before Christmas and the later than usual opening of schools in the populous Gauteng province depressed results in the second half of the year, which although higher than last year were lower than expected.
